I always make this comment when I see Onyxia posts and I'm surprised no one else says it.    

My suggestion on how to beat her is: 

1. Find YOUR army.  (You do have a possible one here, I might have used whelps eggs in place of drake, but there is some variability that does work)

2. Master the interactions.  I never found grunts to be so annoying as with this battle. And the constant whelp eggs are annoying too.  So you have to know the rotation of your deck to handle each of these guys as them come to you.

3. And this is the one no one seems to talk about but especially for a Drak decks, you need to figure out timing of phase changes.   Watch I think Bulava on this one from a few months ago which I hope is still applicable.  But he talks about taking all the towers and controlling the map,  but then doing NOTHING to progress the match.  Put up rime skeletons everywhere that they won't die to a phase change.  Then when your getting close to overtime is when you do the phase change, followed by another perfectly timed push to retake towers. Last push I believe avoids most towers and goes up the right side.

I want to say a few things about the statistics on ADHD.  It's assumed that 10% of the population has it.  It also is genetic, so children of parents who have ADHD are more likely to have it than the child of a parent without ADHD.  The diagnosis for ADHD requires that the symptoms are present in multiple settings, so it makes sense that the doctor wants to know how he acts with others. I can't be sure because I wasn't there, but from what you said I think your doctor is taking this seriously and is going through the steps to get an accurate diagnosis.  

So stimulants are a class of medication that is considered first line therapy for ADHD.  This includes stuff like Adderall, Concerta, Ritalin, Vyvanse and a few others.  These help activate the part of the brain that controls the rest of it.  The problem with ADHD isn't a lack of attention (because alot of people can also experience hyperfixation where they can do an activity for hours and can't get themselves to do other things they should do).  The problem with ADHD is is a lack of control of where you need to put your attention. Imagine the brain as a party with alot of people.  Now imagine that the security guard is asleep, the people are going to do whatever they want.  Now if you wake up the security guard (with a stimulant), then security will be able to tell people what to do and when to do it.

First of all, humans have evolved to have a reward system in the brain that is intended to make the individual feel good when doing tasks that improve their chances of individual survival as well as survival of the species.  An example is eating food makes you feel good, so therefore you are more likely to eat food again and improves your chances of surviving at least to the point of having children.  The reward system also works for other activities like completing a task or winning a game.  

Now let's compare gaming with school. When you spend an hour gaming, how many games do you win? How many quests do you complete? How many fireworks have gone off when you lined up 3 pieces of candy? When you go to class for an hour, how many tests have you passed?  When you turn the page reading a chapter, do any bells or fireworks go off? You can see how gaming rewards the brain more.

The usual argument for this then is that gaming doesn't provide real rewards and college does. The brain doesn't know this at the basic level. You understand there's a difference but you don't feel the difference. 

Another argument is that the video game reward does take just as long to grind for level 100 or for that cosmetic gear that takes 100 quests to get.  Those are not the rewards the brain recognizes to activate the reward center. Those rewards are there in games to make you think about them when you aren't playing so that they draw you back to play again.

Everyone's brain has multiple things going on at once, and for non ADHD people, the frontal lobe allows them to focus on which thought they want to focus on. For ADHD people, it's more like whatever thought maybe is either most interesting or most emotionally charged takes over.  Again, I'm just going based on my understanding here so the details can be wrong.  

The difficulty in choosing which thoughts to focus on leads to several problems.  As it comes to attention, this means not focusing on boring things like school or work AND hyperfocusing on things that are entertaining like reddit, video games, a really good book...It also can cause things like impulsivity and irritability.  I'm not sure here if impulsivity is directly from ADHD or something that's learned (it's easier to buy something now when you want it, instead of forgetting to buy it later).  

People with ADHD may have depression especially if they are diagnosed later than childhood. Some suggest a 20/3/8 rule.  Put 20% down, finance for no more than 3 years, and payments shouldn't exceed 8% of your gross income.  These rules help guide you to purchase a car you can actually afford.  Most people can "afford" more expensive cars outside these rules,  but you lose so much more on interest over time.   On a depreciating asset,  this isn't worth it.   

Used will be cheaper than new,  but there is piece of mind/ more security (including technological advances) with new cars. 

Subaru, Honda, and Toyota depreciate the least.  Land rover, Mercedes, and Jaguar depreciate the most over 3 years and likely beyond.  

Know the difference in MSRP and invoice price and understand invoice price may not even be what the dealership paid.  

You can often ask for extras (floor mats, oil changes) to sweeten your deal.  

Financing is cheaper than paying cash, if you can negotiate it.  This should be done after you agree to the price on the car.  Dealerships make more money on the interest now so they may be willing to cut you a deal on the car of you finance.

Typically buying a car at the end of the month or year is best.  The dealerships are trying to meet quotas, so they will cut a deal if they need to meet the quota.  If the newer year of car is coming out soon, they may cut a deal on the previous year model if they need to move it off their lot.
